note: An open evaluation suite for multi-step reasoning, useful as an independent comparison point against a vendor own numbers.
title: Chain-of-Thought Hub: A Continuous Effort to Measure Large Language Models' Reasoning Performance
explain_beginner: This paper introduces an open tool for checking how well language models handle problems that need several reasoning steps. The authors gathered difficult tests and compared many models. They found that bigger models generally reason better. In May 2023, only Claude-v1.3 and PaLM-2 came close to GPT-4, while openly available models trailed. LLaMA-65B was near code-davinci-002, suggesting more development such as training with human feedback could help it approach GPT-3.5-Turbo. This matters because people may rely on these models for complex tasks, so independent comparisons help show which ones are actually capable.
explain_business: This paper offers an independent, public way to compare language models on complex reasoning, rather than relying only on vendors' own claims. The authors compiled difficult tests and found that model size relates to reasoning skill. In May 2023, only Claude-v1.3 and PaLM-2 were close to GPT-4, and open models lagged. LLaMA-65B was near code-davinci-002, so further development could make open models more competitive. For executives, this informs which models to consider and how much to trust vendor reported results. It suggests checking independent evaluations before committing, and watching open progress, especially around base models and human feedback training.
explain_practitioner: The authors built Chain-of-Thought Hub, an openly available evaluation suite for measuring language models on reasoning tasks that require multiple steps. They assembled a set of difficult reasoning benchmarks and used it to track model progress. Their results show that model size tracks with reasoning ability. As of May 2023, Claude-v1.3 and PaLM-2 were the only models comparable to GPT-4, while open models remained behind. LLaMA-65B performed close to code-davinci-002, which suggests that further work, especially better base models and RLHF, could help open efforts close the gap.
